comments.body:
Verb mapping and evidence (basis origin/main 2e81cb9767c1; the baseline is 72 top-level verbs).

Hint mechanism as it exists: `src/rebar/_cli/_help_route.py:49-55` two frozensets form `_REMOVED_SIMPLE_CLI_ALIASES`; `pre_scan` (`:175-176`) routes a hit to `_emit_removed_alias_invalid_choice` (`:139-150`), which builds a throwaway argparse `choices=` parser and lets it fail, printing argparse's `invalid choice: 'x' (choose from ...)` on stderr with exit 2. It does NOT print "use X instead" today; that text lives only in `docs/exit-codes.md:105-108`. Pinned by `tests/unit/test_cli_registry_dispatch.py:459-487`. The epic upgrades the frozensets to a dict `_REMOVED_SPELLINGS: dict[str, str]` and adds the hint line; the existing assertions still hold. Do NOT use `Route.retired=True` for removed verbs: `tests/unit/test_cli_registry.py:92-102` asserts `all(not route.retired for route in ROUTES)`. Removed spellings are deleted from `ROUTES` and listed only in the hint dict.

| Old | New | Hint dict value |
|---|---|---|
| exists | resolve (exit 0 found, 1 not found) | rebar resolve <id>  (exit 0 = found, 1 = not found) |
| format | resolve --display[=auto|canonical|alias|short] | rebar resolve <id> --display[=MODE] |
| check-ac | check <id> --ac | rebar check <id> --ac |
| clarity-check | check <id> --clarity (also check --clarity --stdin) | rebar check <id> --clarity |
| quality-check | check <id> (default = dispatch readiness) | rebar check <id> |
| tag | edit <id> --add-tag=<t> | rebar edit <id> --add-tag=<tag> |
| untag | edit <id> --remove-tag=<t> | rebar edit <id> --remove-tag=<tag> |
| get-file-impact | show <id> --field=file_impact | rebar show <id> --field=file_impact |
| get-verify-commands | show <id> --field=verify_commands | rebar show <id> --field=verify_commands |
| list-descendants | deps <id> --descendants | rebar deps <id> --descendants |
| session-logs | list --type=session_log --sort=-created --limit=N [--full] | rebar list --type=session_log --sort=-created --limit=5 [--full] |
| compact | store compact <id> | rebar store compact <id> |
| compact-all | store compact --all | rebar store compact --all |
| fsck | store fsck | rebar store fsck |
| fsck-recover | store fsck-recover | rebar store fsck-recover |
| doctor | store doctor | rebar store doctor |
| tracker-maintenance | store maintenance | rebar store maintenance |
| tracker-footprint | store footprint | rebar store footprint |
| export | store export | rebar store export |
| import | store import | rebar store import |

Kept flat, unchanged: golden path `init create claim transition ready list search show`; gates `review-plan verify-completion review-code sign-review explain`; families `bridge workflow identity llm config metrics audit`; `idea summary scratch delete archive revert attach-commits link unlink comment edit reopen next-batch deps validate set-file-impact set-verify-commands session-log grounding-info prompt criteria scan-spec sign verify-signature verify-identity verify-opcert verify-commit-ticket trusted-env remote-cert`; `reclaim-collapse` (ADR 0106 epic, untouched); `enrich` (removed by the overlap epic bossy-skittish-foal).

No `attest` group: `verify-commit-ticket` (`.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml:124`), `verify-identity` (`gerrit-verify.yaml:441`, `verify-identity.yml:105`), `verify-opcert` (`verify-identity.yml:115`, `infra/runbooks/mcp-opcert-enforcement-flip.md:40,83,96`) are CI- and runbook-invoked and `verify-identity.yml` is the shipped merge gate (`docs/identity.md:197-199`, ADR 0049). Grouping only the four zero-CI verbs (`sign`, `verify-signature`, `trusted-env`, `remote-cert`) would split one trust family across two spellings. No `llm` regroup: `criteria` is CI-invoked (`.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml:85`), `prompt`/`criteria` already carry subcommands, `scan-spec` is a sibling of the flat gate verbs, `grounding-info` is a one-verb gain. `scratch`, `delete`, `validate` are ticket or content ops, not storage.

Count: 72 - 20 + 2 (`check`, `store`) = 54 top-level (53 after `enrich` goes); 8 `store` members; 62 leaf invocations.

Nested-group mechanism to reuse: `Route.argv_prefix` (`_registry.py:93`) is consumed only by the `argv` adapter (`_execute.py:109`), validated by `prefix_without_argv` (`_registry_checks.py:148-153`), and used by no route today; child `--help` for a family is served by the family handler because `_help_route._NESTED_INTERCEPTS` (`:38-40`) makes `help_requested` accept only a leading `--help` (`:86-88`); the smallest family parser to copy is `_parsers/advanced/audit.py` (39 LOC, argparse `add_subparsers`, uses `build_argument_parser`, satisfying `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_parser_formatter_pinned.py:42`). Only top-level routes get committed help (`scripts/gen_cli_help.py:154` keys by `route.name`), so member help is rendered live.

Generation and gates: `python scripts/gen_cli_help.py` (and `--check`, `:186-215`), `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` (and `--check`); CI: `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml:110-121`, `.github/actions/docs-gates/action.yml:106-120`; tests `tests/unit/test_gen_cli_help.py`, `tests/unit/test_gen_cli_reference.py:56,74,146`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_cli_registry_distribution.py:90-121`. `server.json` and `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` list MCP env vars only; `tests/unit/mcp_library_parity_manifest.json` maps library to MCP only; no CLI impact. `docs/mcp-reference.md` names only `rebar explain` (kept).

Overlap ownership: the overlap epic owns `src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py:427,453` (inside `_intercepts()`, which this epic never edits), `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:65-70`, `_parsers/advanced/enrich.py`, `help/enrich.txt`, its `docs/exit-codes.md` row and `cli-reference.md` section; this epic owns the `_REMOVED_SPELLINGS` dict and the overlap epic appends one `"enrich"` line to it (whichever lands second regenerates both artifacts after rebase; never hand-merge `overview.txt` or `docs/cli-reference.md`). The reconciler epic owns `src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py` and `_parsers/advanced/bridge*.py` plus `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:144-151`; this epic touches neither and leaves `_help_route._BRIDGE_FACTORY:37` and `_NESTED_FAMILY:41-46` as-is (adding only `"store"` to `_NESTED_INTERCEPTS:38-40`). `reclaim-collapse` (`_registry.py:313-320`, `help/reclaim-collapse.txt`) is not moved into `store`.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
The CLI exposes 72 top-level verbs. Twenty of them duplicate an operation that already exists on a golden-path verb, fits one flag, or belongs under a storage-maintenance noun: `exists`/`format` over `resolve`; `check-ac`/`clarity-check`/`quality-check` over one `check`; `tag`/`untag` over `edit`'s existing tag flags; `get-file-impact`/`get-verify-commands` over `show --field`; `list-descendants` over `deps`; `session-logs` over `list`; `compact`/`compact-all`; and the seven tracker verbs that become `rebar store <sub>`. The operator ruled on 2026-09-06: hard cutover with no working aliases, the existing removed-name hint mechanism kept and populated so future releases stay compatible with it, every doc surface accurate, and release notes listing each old-to-new spelling. Golden-path verbs, gate verbs, CI-invoked trust verbs, and existing families keep their spellings; `reclaim-collapse` belongs to the ADR 0106 epic and is untouched. The full mapping table, usage census, and the nested-group mechanism to reuse are recorded in this epic's first comment.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every removed spelling exits 2 with argparse's invalid-choice error plus a hint naming the replacement, and none has a route. Checked by the parametrized dispatch test over the hint registry.
- [ ] Every surviving operation keeps its `--output json` bytes, its exit codes, and its library and MCP names. Checked by the re-targeted goldens, the exit-code doc conformance test, and an unchanged parity manifest.
- [ ] Committed help, the generated CLI reference, the exit-code table, AGENTS.md, the packaged guides, templates, example skills, and MCP client examples teach only the new spellings, and the release notes and a new ADR record every rename. Checked by the docs story's repo-wide grep and the ADR gates.
- [ ] A held-out test keeps removed spellings from returning to any teaching surface and proves each hint's replacement is a live command. Checked by the red-then-green record in that story.

## Child decomposition
- Ticket-verb merges story: delivers criterion 1 for the twelve ticket verbs and criterion 2 for their replacements.
- Store group story: delivers criterion 1 for the nine storage verbs and criterion 2 for the `store` members, depends on the merges story (shared registry and hint dict).
- Documentation story: delivers criterion 3, depends on the store group story.
- Held-out drift test story: delivers criterion 4, depends on the documentation story.
